ind-bazaar-default-11.room: Spice merchant shop or counting room
ind-bazaar-default-11.things: A low wooden divan (gaddi) with a red cylindrical bolster (masnad) and low desk against the north wall; two tiered oil lamp stands (dipastambha) in the northwest and southwest corners; stacks of earthenware pots along the west wall and in the northeast corner; two clusters of four bowls containing colorful spices along the east and south walls; two lidded storage jars in the southeast; an ornate studded wooden door centered on the south wall; walls featuring cusped arched niches and carved jharokha balconies; plain sand-colored floor.
ind-bazaar-default-11.focal: The low divan seating platform with red bolster and desk against the north wall
problems: Doubled asset: the cluster of four spice bowls along the south wall is an exact duplicate of the cluster on the east wall
Doubled asset: the tiered brass lamp stand in the southwest corner is an exact duplicate of the one in the northwest corner
Doubled asset: identical repeated stacks of earthen pots along the west wall
Clipping: the spice bowls on the south wall intersect and clip directly into the wall panel
Misalignment: the central north wall panel behind the divan is mismatched in height and trim with the adjacent wall sections
Sacred object out of place: traditional ritual tiered temple lamps (dipastambhas) placed casually on the floor of a spice trade/storage room
Out of place / incomplete: featureless sand floor inside an otherwise ornate, formal stone interior with no rug or finished flooring

ind-durbar-default-11.culture: Middle Eastern / Islamic (Mughal or Ottoman inspired)
ind-durbar-default-11.things: Six low divans/couches with striped bolster pillows (three along the north wall, two along the south wall, one in the south-east corner); an ornate canopied throne against the east wall; a small striped rug with a central diamond motif lying off-center on the terracotta tile floor; four ornate golden censers/braziers (three along the east wall and one in the south-west corner); and red-and-gold paneled walls with cusped arches and carved wooden jali screens.
